title: Evaluation of Scaled Segmented Channel MOSFETs for Analog/RF Applications | EECS at UC Berkeley
content: Evaluation of Scaled Segmented Channel MOSFETs for Analog/RF Applications | EECS at UC Berkeley Evaluation of Scaled Segmented Channel MOSFETs for Analog/RF Applications Lars Tatum EECS Department, University of California, Berkeley Technical Report No. UCB/EECS-2020-84 May 28, 2020 http://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/TechRpts/2020/EECS-2020-84.pdf While advanced transistor structures have enabled gate length scaling below 20 nanometers and consequently enabled digital integrated circuits to increase in complexity with advancements in semiconductor manufacturing, they have not enabled similar improvement in analog IC performance due to degraded transconductance and increased gate leakage. Because of this, most analog ICs are manufactured using older-generation technology with long-channel transistors. The long channel length limits the transistor maximum oscillation frequency, however. In this study, technology computer-aided design simulations are used to assess the potential benefits of a quasi-planar segmented-channel transistor (SegFET) design for enhanced analog/RF performance, based on a mature 65 nm generation CMOS transistor technology.
